newsitem.title: USA: Amnesty made to Miami residents with street loot.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty made to Miami residents with street loot.

text.p: Police on Thursday gave Miami residents 48 hours to return hundreds of thousands of dollars that rained onto an impoverished neighborhood after an armored car crashed.
The no-questions-asked amnesty, to end at midday (1700 GMT) on Saturday, was announced a day after an accident that some residents of the inner city Overtown neighborhood called a gift from God.

During the Wednesday morning rush hour, a Brink's armored security truck believed to be carrying $3.7 million flipped on a highway overpass, cracked open and sent a river of bundled currency and coins on to a street below.

Some neighborhood residents grabbed bags and rakes to scoop up loot while others scrambled on the ground on their hands and knees in a carnival atmosphere amid chortles of "Finders keepers, losers weepers."

Brink's officials would not say how much money was lost before police arrived but police said they had heard estimates of $500,000 or even more. One firefighter found a bag holding $300,000 after the official retrieval began.
By Thursday, the carnival atmosphere was largely gone, as police tried to track down the missing money. Hours after the amnesty began, none of the money had been turned in.

"We are going door to door talking to folks and we are appealing to their morals, to tell us what they know or to give us the money if they have it," Lt. Bill Schwartz, a Miami police spokesman, said.
He said officers were also warning residents that a sudden windfall could make them the victims of crime. "If we are looking for money you can bet that the bad guys are too," Schwartz said.
